title: Trump Claims '100% Control' of Hormuz, Demands Iran Pay War Reparations
detail: Speaking from the Oval Office, President Trump said the US Navy has swept the Strait of Hormuz clear of mines and now holds '100%' control of the waterway, describing the ongoing US naval presence as a blockade restricting Iranian access. Trump said Iran should pay reparations for damage he claimed it has caused over the past 50 years, introducing reparations as a new flashpoint in the standoff. In response, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said the strait will not reopen until Washington lifts its naval blockade and sanctions, withdraws US forces from the region, pays Iran war reparations, and unfreezes Iranian assets — leaving the two sides' conditions for a settlement further apart than before.

media.caption: Trump claims '100% control' of the Strait of Hormuz and demands Iran pay reparations

title: Trump Pivots to 'Operation Economic Fury' Sanctions Campaign as Iran Calls Pressure Ineffective
detail: The Trump administration doubled down on 'Operation Economic Fury,' its financial-pressure campaign against Iran running since April 16, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent saying Iran's shadow banking system is 'buckling' and calling sanctions the 'financial equivalent' of a bombing campaign. Trump said Iran is 'broke, totally broke.' Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei rejected the pressure campaign, saying repeated sanctions rounds — the eighth targeting Iran's alleged shadow-banking network in 2026 — only make a diplomatic solution 'less likely' and reflect Washington's pattern of 'increasing the dose' when sanctions fail to produce results.

media.caption: Trump pivots back to sanctions for Iran as other strategies to end his war fizzle

title: US Helicopter Fires Hellfire Missiles to Disable Blockade-Running Cargo Ship Vela Nova
detail: A US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles into the engine room and steering gear of the Panama-flagged cargo ship Vela Nova in the Gulf of Oman, roughly 71 nautical miles off the coast of Pakistan, after its civilian crew ignored repeated warnings and continued sailing toward an Iranian port in violation of the US naval blockade. CENTCOM said the vessel is 'no longer transiting to Iran.' A resulting fire was extinguished; all crew were accounted for with no injuries reported. It was the third vessel the US has forcibly disabled since reimposing the blockade on July 14; CENTCOM said it had redirected 55 commercial vessels attempting to run the blockade as of Aug 11.

media.caption: US forces fire on cargo vessel it said sought to break the Iran blockade

title: Houthi 'Double-Tap' Missile Strikes Kill 6 in First Fatal Red Sea Shipping Attack Since War Began
detail: Houthi forces fired three ballistic missiles at the Egyptian-owned, Tanzania-flagged cargo ship Tihamah near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait off Yemen's coast, sparking a fire and killing four crew members (three Pakistani nationals, one Indonesian). As Yemeni coast guard personnel moved to evacuate the dead and wounded, a second missile struck the rescue operation, killing two more rescuers and wounding three. Ten people were wounded in total. It was the first fatal Houthi attack on commercial shipping since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran on Feb 28. Houthi-aligned media claimed the vessel was carrying Saudi military equipment but did not name the ship in an official statement.

media.caption: Six killed in Houthi 'double-tap' attack on ship near Bab al-Mandeb
